subject: biology
title: Inside the Living Cell
welcome_lead: Zoom down to microscopic scale and explore the parts that build every living thing.
meta_desc: KS3 Biology adventure exploring animal and plant cell parts, structure and function.
final_note: You now know the working parts of a living cell — the foundation of all biology.

walkthroughs.body_html: Animal cells contain a nucleus that controls activities, cytoplasm where reactions happen, a cell membrane that controls what enters and leaves, and mitochondria that release energy.
Plant cells have everything animal cells have plus a cell wall for support, chloroplasts for photosynthesis and a large vacuole filled with cell sap.
Both share nucleus, cytoplasm, membrane and mitochondria. Only plants have a wall, chloroplasts and a permanent vacuole. This lets plants stay rigid and make their own food.

mcqs.q: What distinguishes the innate from the adaptive immune response?
options: Innate immunity only works in children; adaptive only works in adults.
Ribosomes synthesise amino acids from scratch using the mRNA as a template.
Innate immunity attacks viruses and adaptive attacks bacteria.
Innate is fast, non-specific, and has no memory; adaptive is slower initially, highly specific, and forms memory cells.

mcqs.q: What is the role of the guide RNA in CRISPR-Cas9?
options: Innate immunity only works in children; adaptive only works in adults.
Guide RNA is the new sequence that gets inserted into the genome.
It directs Cas9 to the specific DNA sequence to cut by base-pairing with the target.
Guide RNA is the enzyme that cuts the DNA.

mcqs.q: What reads the mRNA codons during translation?
options: tRNA molecules carrying specific amino acids — their anticodons pair with mRNA codons at the ribosome.
Ribosomes synthesise amino acids from scratch using the mRNA as a template.
Guide RNA is the enzyme that cuts the DNA.
DNA directly reads the codons on mRNA and adds amino acids.
